title: Dinner refuses to land
topic: In Spring, in Harris County north of Houston, Uber Eats customers became the first in the country to get food by Zipline drone, which hovers high over the yard and lowers the order in a pod on a tether while remote pilots can still override a flight.
hook: Dinner is coming. It refuses to land.

treatment.logline: A Spring backyard dog guards the gate for the delivery driver, and dinner arrives from the one direction nobody guards, a drone that hovers high and lowers a pod on a string.
treatment.cold_open: A dog crouches at a backyard gate under pines, tail stiff, nose at the latch. A shadow slides across the grass behind it, its ears swivel, and an orange pod on a tether drops into the top of the frame.
treatment.turn: Fully robotic and under 10 minutes are the companies' own words. A remote pilot can still override, Spring was first only for Uber Eats by Zipline, Zipline has already made 1 million deliveries around Dallas, and 1 million a day is a target drawn as dashed ghosts.
treatment.button: Back in the yard a hand takes the sack, the empty pod rises up its line, and the dog finally barks, straight up at a dot in the sky.

hero.name: the delivery drone with a face and its orange pod
hero.why: a round white drone with long wings, a visor face that squints into rain and listens for planes, and a little orange pod with eyes that rides a tether down. No earlier film has drawn a delivery drone or a tethered drop.

scenes.vo: A dog guards this gate for the delivery driver. Dinner is coming. It refuses to land.

draw.subject: the dog
draw.action: crouches nose to the gate latch with its tail stiff while a shadow slides across the grass behind it
draw.emotion: the dog is alert, ears forward

draw.subject: the orange pod
draw.action: drops into the top of the frame on a thin tether as the dog's ears swivel up

scenes.vo: In Spring, north of Houston, people became the first in the country to order Uber Eats by Zipline drone, on Tuesday, November 17th. Open the app, and pick by drone on the home screen.

draw.subject: the customer
draw.action: steps out the screen door onto the porch and lifts her phone

visual_events.label: First for Uber Eats by drone

draw.subject: a ribbon banner
draw.action: unrolls over the porch roof with a pop as the customer grins

draw.subject: a calendar tag
draw.action: flips onto the ribbon banner and lands on the 17th

draw.subject: her thumb
draw.action: taps the big round by drone button and it lights orange with a ring pulsing out

scenes.vo: Then the drone picks up the order, and flies it to the customer.

draw.subject: the cook
draw.action: carries the sealed sack out the back door and clips it into the orange pod hanging on its tether

draw.subject: the pod
draw.action: zips straight up its tether with the sack showing in its window
draw.emotion: the cook leans back and watches it go, doubtful

scenes.vo: As it takes off, its weather sensors measure the wind.

draw.subject: the drone
draw.action: rises over the restaurant roof with the pod reeled up under its belly
draw.emotion: the cook at the back door shields her eyes

draw.subject: the drone's face
draw.action: squints as white wind ribbons bend around its nose and it tilts into them

scenes.vo: It cruises at about 300 feet, at up to 70 miles an hour. It can carry eight pounds as far as 10 miles.

draw.subject: the drone
draw.action: streaks over pine tops and rooftops while its shadow races across the street below
draw.emotion: a neighbour on the sidewalk points up

draw.subject: speed lines
draw.action: stretch behind the drone and a counter ticks up to 70

draw.subject: a ring on the map
draw.action: spreads out 10 miles from the restaurant pin while a scale needle swings to eight pounds

scenes.vo: Rain doesn't ground it. Small microphones listen for nearby aircraft, as far as 1.25 miles away, the company says.

draw.subject: the drone
draw.action: crosses the rain overhead while a neighbour's umbrella fills the foreground and tips back to watch

draw.subject: the drone's microphones
draw.action: glow and send rings out until they touch a small plane far off and the drone's eyes turn to it

draw.subject: the small plane
draw.action: banks away up the sky while the drone eases aside and nods

scenes.vo: Over the yard, it never lands. It hovers, and the pod comes down on a tether.

draw.subject: the drone
draw.action: brakes high over the backyard and holds, tiny against the sky above the pines
draw.emotion: the customer looks up from the porch

draw.subject: the pod
draw.action: slides down the tether past the pine tops with the folded sack showing in its window, swinging gently, as the dog's eyes climb the line

scenes.vo: Zipline says it stays roughly 330 feet up to deliver. Other delivery drones average 32 feet. Its chief executive, Keller Cliffton, says staying that high keeps it very quiet.

draw.subject: a measuring tape
draw.action: unspools from the lawn all the way up to the drone at the top of the frame

draw.subject: a second drone
draw.action: pops in barely above the pine tops at the 32 foot tick, loud lines buzzing off it
draw.emotion: the customer winces at the low one

draw.subject: a quote card
draw.action: slides up beside the dog with the words very quiet on it

draw.subject: the dog
draw.action: lowers its ears, yawns and sits down on the grass

scenes.vo: Zipline calls the system fully robotic and autonomous. An Uber executive says it reaches homes in under 10 minutes. Those are the companies' own words.

draw.subject: a big card
draw.action: stamps down with FULLY ROBOTIC while the little drone puffs up proudly beside it

draw.subject: the customer
draw.action: holds up her phone timer under a big stopwatch that sweeps toward 10 minutes and freezes as quote marks slam in

draw.subject: the stopwatch
draw.action: turns to a dashed outline, a claim and not a measurement
draw.emotion: the customer raises an eyebrow, skeptical

scenes.vo: A person still watches. Zipline's remote pilots can override a flight path if there is a safety issue.

draw.subject: the remote pilot
draw.action: leans in to a wide screen where the drone's dot moves along its path

draw.subject: the pilot's hand
draw.action: hovers over the override key as a yellow frame flashes and the path bends

scenes.vo: Drone delivery is new to Spring. It is not new to Zipline. In Round Rock, a high school drone team placed and received the first order.

draw.subject: two drone team students
draw.action: run across a schoolyard looking up and pointing

visual_events.at_phrase: It is not new to Zipline
visual_events.label: Not new to Zipline

draw.subject: a parade of orange pods
draw.action: streams across the sky over the schoolyard as the students spin to follow it

draw.subject: the pod
draw.action: comes down its tether into the students' raised hands, nothing touching down

scenes.vo: Zipline says it has already made 1 million drone deliveries around Dallas alone.

draw.subject: a counter
draw.action: rolls up to 1,000,000 in the corner over a Dallas-area street at dusk and lands with a thump

draw.subject: a dozen pods
draw.action: come down tethers into a dozen backyards at once while neighbours look up
draw.emotion: a neighbour waves at the sky

scenes.vo: The goal is 1 million deliveries a day with Uber by 2029. That is a target, not a count.

draw.subject: dashed ghost drones
draw.action: fill the sky above the restaurant in rows
draw.emotion: the cook at the back door looks up, amazed

draw.subject: the ghost drones
draw.action: flicker to empty outlines while one real drone flies through them

scenes.vo: Back in Spring, a hand takes the sack, and nobody has to tip. The dog still barks, just at the sky now.

draw.subject: the customer
draw.action: unclips the sack from the pod and lifts it, steam curling out

draw.subject: the empty pod
draw.action: zips back up its line toward the sky

draw.subject: the dog
draw.action: plants its feet and barks straight up at a dot leaving the sky
